articles.title: Human interferon-α autoantibody development broadens reactivity and enables functional synergy.
articles.abstract: NA: Neutralizing autoantibodies against interferon-α (IFN-α) are associated with severe viral infections but may improve outcomes in IFN-α-driven autoimmunity. How these antibodies emerge, mature, and function at the molecular level remains unclear. Here, we tracked development of plasma neutralizing activity against all 12 IFN-αs in multiple human donors over years. Plasma neutralization frequently initiated with narrow IFN-α specificity, often against IFN-α8, but increased in breadth and potency with individual kinetics. Monoclonal antibody analyses revealed that affinity maturation generated epitope-specific antibody classes, highlighting parallel emergence of subtype-restricted and broadly reactive antibodies. Biophysical and structural characterization of human antibody-IFN-α complexes uncovered determinants of initial specificity and breadth development. Antibodies engaging non-competing, neutralizing epitopes acted co-operatively to block IFN-α signaling, and some combinations triggered Fc-effector functions via cell surface IFN-α:IFNAR2 interactions that may eliminate IFN-α-responsive cells. Our findings reveal features shaping anti-IFN-α autoantibody repertoires and synergistic mechanisms that amplify their potency and pathogenic potential.

articles.title: Granzyme K is a driver of age-related tissue remodeling and functional decline independently of age-associated immune dysfunction.
articles.abstract: NA: Aging is characterized by progressive tissue and organ decline, with chronic low-grade inflammation (inflammaging) implicated as a central driver. Granzyme K (GzmK), a serine protease that is markedly upregulated in aged memory CD8+ T cells, is proposed to be a central mediator of both immune and organismal aging. Using young and aged GzmK-/- mice, we showed that GzmK was dispensable for the major hallmarks of immune aging, including T cell dysfunction, but was a critical driver of age-related tissue decline. Despite persistent immune aging phenotypes, GzmK deficiency markedly attenuated organ aging, effectively uncoupling immune and tissue aging. In the kidney, this was associated with reduced complement deposition, whereas in the liver, improved function and reduced fibrosis occurred independently of complement, coinciding instead with increased decorin and reduced pro-fibrotic TGF-β signaling. These findings identify GzmK as a tissue-specific driver of organismal aging but not immune aging or systemic inflammaging.

articles.title: TIGIT and PD-L1 co-blockade promotes dendritic cell-dependent production of non-exhausted CD8+ T cells.
articles.abstract: NA: Combination immunotherapy targeting the coinhibitory molecules TIGIT and PD-L1 promotes non-exhausted CD8+ T cell differentiation in cancer. Because anti-TIGIT efficacy requires Fc binding, we investigated the role of Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-expressing myeloid cells in the mechanism of action. Conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) were required for therapeutic efficacy. Transcriptional profiling of intratumoral myeloid cells revealed an FcγR+ cDC type-1 (cDC1)-like activation state characterized by elevated costimulatory ligands for CD28 (CD80/CD86) and CD226 (PVR) that was enriched in Fc-active anti-TIGIT combination-treated tumors. Therapy-expanded CD8+ T cells expressed CD28 and upregulated CD226 upon treatment. Mechanistically, CD28 signaling was a prerequisite for therapy-induced CD226 expression on T cells, and cDC-derived PVR promoted CD226-mediated non-exhausted T cell differentiation. Type I interferon (IFN-I), induced through FcγR engagement, maintained and amplified the FcγR+ cDC1-like state, and exogenous IFN-I rescued anti-tumor immunity upon Fc-inert anti-TIGIT and anti-PD-L1 combination. Thus, Fc-active anti-TIGIT and anti-PD-L1 therapy promotes a sequential costimulatory cascade centered on cDCs, amplified by IFN-I signaling.

articles.title: Frankenstein protein assembled by mRNA trans-splicing promotes cytokine release.
articles.abstract: NA: Trans-splicing of pre-mRNAs to produce alternate proteins is known to occur in unicellular and invertebrate organisms; yet whether such events occur and produce functional proteins in mammals remains unclear. In a recent issue of Nature, macrophages polarized to an inflammatory state were found to produce several chimeric RNAs through trans-splicing with consequences for the inflammatory response.

articles.title: Phosphocreatine strengthens CD8+ T cells by remodeling chromatin.
articles.abstract: NA: Metabolites can regulate T cell gene expression and effector function, but how changes in mitochondrial ATP production influence chromatin remodeling remains unclear. In a recent issue of Cell, Ng et al. demonstrate that D-α-hydroxybutyrate (DAHB) increases oxidative phosphorylation and phosphocreatine production, promoting chromatin accessibility and CD8+ T cell effector function to limit tumor growth.

articles.title: Dendritic cells drive next-generation checkpoint blockade immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: NA: Conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s) are key orchestrators of antitumor immunity. In this issue of Immunity, Luri-Rey et al. and Duong et al. show that two next-generation checkpoint strategies act through mature cDC1s, which assemble the costimulatory signals that set CD8⁺ T cell fate and determine therapeutic efficacy.

articles.title: Allergic resident memory finds a skin niche.
articles.abstract: NA: Mechanisms driving allergic relapse in the skin remain poorly defined. In this issue of Immunity, Asahina et al. identify a pathogenic CXCR6+ subset of skin-resident memory CD4+ T cells that persist after biologic treatment in human atopic dermatitis.

articles.title: The stromal pit crew keeps GCs racing with PD-L1.
articles.abstract: NA: The PD-1/PD-L1 axis is a pivotal yet incompletely understood regulator of germinal center responses. In this issue of Immunity, Akama-Garren et al. demonstrate that PD-L1 expression on stromal cells enhances T-B cell collaborations and humoral immunity.

articles.title: Egg-ception to the rule: Monocyte-derived microglia infiltrate CVOs.
articles.abstract: NA: Circumventricular organs (CVOs) are specialized interfaces between the peripheral circulation and the brain. In this issue of Immunity, Van Hove et al. reveal CVOs as distinct immune niches that shape brain macrophage identity. These environments generate specialized macrophage phenotypes and enable fetal monocytes to adopt bona fide microglial identities, thereby demonstrating how local tissue context can influence immune cell fate.

articles.title: Tumor-to-dendritic cell reprogramming induces immunogenic lymphoid structures across cancers.
articles.abstract: NA: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in tumors are associated with improved responses to immunotherapy. Here, we examined the impact of type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s) in TLS formation. Reprogrammed tumor cells into cDC1-like cells remodeled the tumor microenvironment and induced immunogenic TLSs (imgTLSs) across melanoma, colon, bladder, breast, and pancreatic cancer models with distinct genetic backgrounds. cDC1-like cells activated lymphotoxin, TNF, and interferon programs and engaged early with T cells through MHC class I and CD40 signaling to induce imgTLSs containing BCL6+ germinal centers, independently of endogenous cDC1s. Intratumoral positioning shaped distinct cDC1-like cell states, with DC-LAMP+ CCR7+ migratory cDC1s nucleating niches enriched in CD4+, CD8+ T cells, and B cells in mouse and human tumors. ImgTLSs sustained B and T cell responses and promoted systemic immunity through expansion of shared clonotypes in distant, untreated tumors. Our findings outline the spatial organization, signaling programs and interactions of cDC1-like cells that initiate intratumoral lymphoid structures and establish cellular reprogramming as a strategy toward overcoming resistance to immunotherapy.

articles.title: Mitochondrial DNA abundance is a determinant of immunogenic cell death in cancer.
articles.abstract: NA: Cells experiencing mitochondrial stress can undergo apoptosis or cell death that triggers innate immune activation. We examined the mechanisms determining these distinct outcomes in cancer. Abundant mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and high expression of the cGAS-STING pathway were features of KRAS-mutant cancers. In a pharmacological screen, MEK inhibitor (MEKi) effectively induced mtDNA release into the cytosol in KRAS-mutant cancer cells. However, MEKi also induced PRKN-mediated mitophagy, which limited mtDNA release by eliminating damaged mitochondria. Inhibition of mitophagy sustained mtDNA efflux and amplified cGAS-STING signaling. Mechanistically, PRKN-mediated mitophagy restrained mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) to limit mtDNA efflux. The balance between mtDNA and cytochrome c (cyt.c) release defined two immunologically distinct outcomes: immunogenic cell death (ICD) and apoptosis. In preclinical models, combined inhibition of MEK and mitophagy induced robust dendritic cell (DC) activation and promoted CD8+ T cell-mediated antitumor immunity. Consistently, PRKN expression negatively correlated with immune infiltration in human cancers. Collectively, these findings provide a rationale for combination strategies targeting mitochondrial dynamics to augment antitumor immunity.

articles.title: Growth factor VEGF-B sustains intestinal Tfh cell stemness to restrict Taurinivorans outgrowth and microbiota-driven obesity.
articles.abstract: NA: Autocrine signaling through vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR-1) reprograms T cell metabolism upon TCR stimulation. We found that mice bearing conditional deletion of Flt1 (encoding VEGFR-1) in T cells developed spontaneous obesity with advancing age. Analyses of lymphoid and metabolic tissues identified a VEGFR-1+ T follicular helper (Tfh) population in Peyer's patches and mesenteric lymph nodes. Flt1 deletion impaired Tfh fitness and reduced secretory IgA in the gut, resulting in unrestricted expansion of the pathobiont Taurinivorans. Taurinivorans overgrowth depleted host taurine, which drove obesity via suppressed adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis. Mechanistically, a VEGFR-1-AKT signaling axis promoted Tfh cell stemness by limiting p53-mediated senescence. This Tfh-microbiota-obesity pathway was also observed in diet-induced obese mice and in humans. Oral administration of IgA reduced Taurinivorans and alleviated adiposity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this axis. Tfh cell senescence impairs IgA production, disrupting gut microbial homeostasis, with consequences to host metabolic disease.

articles.title: T cell cross-priming by PD-L1+ type 1 conventional dendritic cells mediates the antitumor efficacy of a PD-L1×4-1BB bispecific antibody.
articles.abstract: NA: Bispecific antibodies that conditionally engage costimulatory receptors aim to enhance antitumor T cell immunity while limiting systemic toxicity. We investigated mechanisms underlying the clinical performance of a PD-L1×4-1BB bispecific antibody. Therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1×4-1BB was largely independent of PD-L1 expression on malignant cells but waned in Batf3-/- mice or upon depletion of type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s). cDC1-specific deletion of PD-L1 markedly limited tumor control. PD-L1×4-1BB enhanced proliferation of tumor-antigen-specific CD8+ T cells through mechanisms dependent on cross-presentation, the presence of interleukin (IL)-12, 4-1BB costimulation, and CD40L-mediated cDC1 licensing. PD-L1×4-1BB increased cDC1-T cell contacts, which promoted transcriptional programs associated with T cell activation and proliferation. Treated tumors exhibited increased infiltration and spatial proximity of cDC1s and activated CD8+ T cells. Accordingly, increasing dendritic-cell abundance via Flt3L further enhanced tumor control. Thus, cDC1-T cell interactions are central to PD-L1×4-1BB activity, with antigen cross-presentation, dendritic-cell licensing, and IL-12 and 4-1BB costimulation converging to promote antitumor immunity.

articles.title: PD-L1 expression in germinal centers promotes humoral immunity by restricting T follicular regulatory cell differentiation.
articles.abstract: NA: Germinal center (GC) responses generate humoral immunity through coordinated interactions between B cells and T follicular helper (TFH) and T follicular regulatory (TFR) cells. Despite high expression of PD-1 by TFH and TFR cells, the function of its ligand PD-L1 in the GC is unclear. Here, we show an immunogenic role for PD-L1 via tuning T-B collaboration to promote humoral immunity. Integrated analyses of secondary lymphoid organs (SLOs) revealed that B cell zone reticular cells (BRCs), including follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), expressed PD-L1. BRC expression of PD-L1 facilitated GC formation and enabled loss of B cell tolerance in autoantibody disease. Mechanistically, BRC-specific deletion of PD-L1 enhanced TFH cell production of Sostdc1 and TFR cell differentiation, destabilizing T-B contacts in the GC. Patient-derived tumor biopsies indicated that a tumor-infiltrating TFH SOSTDC1 signature inversely correlated with immunotherapy responsiveness. These findings reveal a non-canonical immunogenic role for PD-L1 in the GC and suggest that augmenting B cell responses could improve the efficacy of PD-L1 blockade.

articles.title: A microbiome-reactive TMIGD2hi Th17 subset is spatially enriched at the intestinal epithelium and expanded in inflammatory bowel disease.
articles.abstract: NA: Subsets of intestinal CD4+ T cells directly recognize commensal bacteria and coordinate tolerance versus protective immunity. Our limited understanding of CD4+ T cell specificities and corresponding functional phenotypes has created a barrier to deciphering the mechanisms of mucosal homeostasis and inflammation mediated by the adaptive immune system. To address this, we leveraged an immunodominant Bacteroidetes epitope in SusC to perform single-cell profiling of the SusC-specific and total CD4+ T cell landscapes in intestinal tissues of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). By analyzing phenotypes and T cell receptor specificities in parallel, we uncovered phenotypic diversification of T helper 17 (Th17) cells in IBD and identified an epithelial-localized, SusC-reactive Th17 subset that is BACH2lo, GZMAhi, and expresses the costimulatory receptor TMIGD2. Together, our results highlight the utility of tracking commensal-specific T cell responses to define specialized subsets of Th17 cells associated with loss of tolerance to the microbiome.

articles.title: Human brain cellular xenografts in neuroimmunology and beyond.
articles.abstract: NA: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a platform to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. HBCXs involve transplanting human pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, glia, or organoids into immunodeficient mice to model human disease. These models have revealed human-specific cellular and molecular phenotypes, developmental trajectories, and disease mechanisms that would otherwise be inaccessible in traditional in vitro systems and animal models. They also provide a scalable, genetically editable framework for functional genomics studies, drug testing, and biomarker discovery. Given the pronounced species differences in microglia and other tissue-resident brain macrophages and their central involvement in neurodegenerative disease, these models also provide an in vivo platform to interrogate human neuroimmunology. In selected settings, they may help guide future cell-based therapeutic strategies. This review provides an overview of the current applications, discusses the challenges and limitations, and highlights future avenues of HBCXs in neuroimmunology and translational research.

articles.title: NF-κB phosphorylation controls enhancer selection to shape the inflammatory gene program.
articles.abstract: NA: Inflammatory transcriptional responses mediated by NF-κB are diverse despite similar upstream activation signals. Because phosphorylation of the NF-κB subunit RelA/p65 promotes interaction with co-activators CREB-binding protein/E1A binding protein p300 (CBP/p300) and selectively affects gene expression, we asked whether this modification distinguishes regulatory architectures underlying distinct immune functions. In macrophages carrying a Rela Ser276Ala mutation, p65 phosphorylation at serine 276 (S276) was dispensable for NF-κB binding to primed enhancers but essential for recruitment to nucleosome-occluded regions lacking pre-bound transcription factors (TFs) and activating histone marks. Such latent enhancers required phosphorylated NF-κB to recruit CBP/p300, promote histone acetylation, and open chromatin. Genes linked to these enhancers, including inflammatory mediators, were selectively impaired in S276A macrophages. Although antiviral responses remained intact, Rela Ser276Ala mice resisted endotoxin shock but were susceptible to bacterial infection. Thus, NF-κB responses are functionally partitioned by enhancer architecture: phosphorylation-sensitive sites define a latent enhancer compartment with NF-κB-dominated regulatory architecture, whereas primed sites are embedded in broader networks of lineage-determining and inducible TFs, yielding distinct biological outputs.

articles.title: Embracing macrophage complexity for research and translation.
articles.abstract: NA: Macrophages are among the most versatile differentiated cell types in the body, serving as key regulators of tissue development, homeostasis, inflammation, repair, and immunity. Their functional diversity cannot be captured by fixed subsets, binary activation states, or single-marker definitions. Macrophage identity emerges instead from the integration of developmental origin, tissue niche, epigenetic history, local environmental cues, and disease-associated signals. Advances in single-cell genomics, spatial profiling, epigenomics, in vivo perturbation, and computational modeling now show that this behavior is organized through modular gene programs, so that any given macrophage state is best described as a weighted combination of program activities rather than a discrete label. We argue that embracing this modular architecture matters not only for annotation but for therapy: macrophage-directed interventions will require defining disease-associated states, identifying surface-accessible entry points into them, and rewiring the underlying programs with spatial and temporal precision.
